headline: Oakland's City Council has unanimously approved a 45-day pause on new data centre approvals.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered to 4: the council vote took place on 6 Oct 2026, before 7 Oct, so the item is stale; the article was read in full.
importance_line: It matters to Oakland residents worried about utility bills, rents and the local environment, and to developers, because the pause gives the city time to study data centres and update its rules, but it is temporary and can be extended.
summary: The Oaklandside reports that Oakland's City Council voted unanimously on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, an older event carried here as a follow-up, for a 45-day moratorium on approvals for new data centres. Oakland City Council member Carroll Fife, who wrote the proposal, says the pause gives the city time to study data centre impacts and update its planning and building codes, and a local coalition counts at least 26 California cities considering or passing similar pauses.
